blurb:
China Great Wall is the kind of neighborhood Chinese spot you're glad exists. It's in a strip mall on Sandy Plains Road and it doesn't try to be anything other than what it is: reliable, familiar Chinese food at a price that makes sense for a weeknight. Good for takeout when you don't feel like cooking, or a quick sit-down dinner with the family.

The menu covers all the classics you'd expect. It's consistent and the portions are solid for the price. When you just want General Tso's or fried rice and you want it done right without a lot of fuss, this is the place.

Note that they open later on Sundays at 3pm, so plan accordingly if you're thinking about an early weekend dinner.

blurb:
Sometimes you just want to feed a group of people without any drama about the menu, and Pacific Buffet handles that pretty well. It's an all-you-can-eat spot out on Chastain Meadows that covers a lot of ground: sushi, tempura, and American fare all in one run through the line. Good for families with picky eaters or when you've got a group that can't agree on a cuisine.

The sushi is what gets mentioned most in reviews, and it's solid for a buffet. The tempura is worth grabbing while it's fresh. For the price, it's hard to argue with the value, especially for lunch.

It's a no-frills setup and nobody's pretending otherwise. Go in knowing what it is and you'll leave happy.

blurb:
If you've got kids who need to burn energy or a group looking for something to do that isn't just dinner, Andretti is worth knowing about. It's a big indoor complex on Roswell Road with multi-level go-kart tracks, arcade games, and food service all under one roof. Good for birthday parties, group outings, or just a Friday night when you want something more than a movie.

The go-karts are the main draw and they're genuinely fun for older kids and adults alike. There's also a full food and drink menu on site, so you can eat there without leaving the building.

Fair warning though: this place has a lot of moving parts and the service can be inconsistent depending on when you go and how busy it is. A few reviews mention slow or inattentive staff during peak hours. If you're doing a birthday package or a large group, confirm all the details ahead of time and get there knowing what's included. It's a solid option when it's humming, just go in with clear expectations.

blurb:
Hamp and Harry's is right on Roswell Street near the Square, and it's the kind of spot you end up at when you want a real dinner out rather than just grabbing food. Good for date night, a night out with friends, or when someone is visiting and you want to take them somewhere that feels like a Marietta place. They do a solid brunch on weekends too.

The scallops come up a lot in reviews and they're legit, worth ordering if you're into seafood. The cocktail menu is there if you want drinks, though a few folks have noted the presentation is nothing fancy. The decor is well done and they go all in for seasonal themes, which is a fun touch.

One thing to know going in: it runs a bit pricey for what it is. The food is good and the service is generally attentive, but it's worth going in with that expectation set so you're not caught off guard by the bill.

blurb:
This place has become a regular stop for me on weekend mornings. It's a Brazilian bakery over on Powers Ferry Road and the vibe is warm and casual. Good for a slow morning coffee, a quick bite before work, or picking up something sweet to bring home. It opens at 6:30am most days, which is earlier than a lot of spots around here.

The Brazilian light bites and traditional baked goods are what you're coming for. The cakes and cookies have a bit of a following, and the pastries move fast on weekends so showing up early is never a bad call.

Prices are very reasonable. It's not a place where you'll drop a lot of money, which makes it easy to become a habit.
